title: Best MCP Servers for Claude in 2026 — Desktop, Claude.ai, and Claude Code
excerpt: Claude is three MCP clients, not one. Here is a practical starter stack for Claude.ai connectors, Claude Desktop, and Claude Code — plus how to search the rest of the catalog from inside the chat.
coverImageAlt: Split view of Claude Desktop connector settings and Claude Code terminal for MCP setup
contentHtml:
People search best MCP servers for Claude and get a single ranked list. That is the wrong answer.

Claude is three MCP surfaces — Claude.ai (web/mobile), Claude Desktop, and Claude Code — with different transport rules. A stdio server that flies in Claude Code will never load as a Claude.ai custom connector. A remote HTTPS server that works in Claude.ai may be the wrong install path for a local coding session.

This guide maps what to install first on each surface, with links into the Influzer directory and a two-minute path to search the rest of the catalog from inside Claude.

The three Claude surfaces (quick map)

SurfaceWhat MCP can runHow you install
Claude.ai (web & mobile)Remote HTTPS onlySettings → Connectors → Custom → Web
Claude DesktopConnectors + local stdioConnectors UI and/or claude_desktop_config.json
Claude Code (CLI)stdio or --transport httpclaude mcp add in the terminal

Full matrix for the Desktop vs CLI split: Claude Code CLI vs Desktop connectors. Org-wide rollout across Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor: One MCP connector, three surfaces.

Rule #1 — start with Discovery

Before you pick Postgres or Playwright, connect Influzer MCP Discovery. It is our official read-only remote MCP — Claude can search 6,000+ servers by capability from inside the chat.

Endpoint: https://www.influzer.ai/mcp/discovery

Setup (Claude tab): /mcp/discovery/setup

  • No OAuth
  • No secrets
  • Works as a Claude.ai custom connector because it is public HTTPS

Try after connect: "Use Influzer to find MCP servers for browser automation" or "Recommend a coding-agent stack with docs lookup."

Listing: /mcp/influzer-mcp-discovery · Intro article: Search MCP without leaving your client.

Remote starter stack (Claude.ai / connectors)

These are the right default when you are on claude.ai or any surface that only accepts HTTPS connectors:

ServerWhy it belongs
Influzer MCP DiscoverySearch the catalog by tool capability
Context7Live library docs — fewer hallucinated APIs
NeonServerless Postgres with a remote MCP path
SentryIssue triage from chat when something breaks

Cap the first install at four to six servers. Claude has to choose among every tool you expose — overlapping tools make wrong picks more likely.

Research stack (Desktop / Claude Code)

Search and scrape are usually local stdio packages. Use them in Desktop or Claude Code, not as Claude.ai connectors unless the vendor ships HTTPS.

  • Exa — neural web search when the agent starts from a question
  • Firecrawl — URL → clean markdown when you already have pages
  • Brave Search — lighter SERP-style search

Exa finds; Firecrawl reads. Many research chats use both. Comparison: MCP vs REST for the broader why, and our topic guide on web scraping MCP.

Coding stack (Claude Code first)

For repo-adjacent work in the terminal:

  • Context7 — framework docs while you edit
  • Playwright — browser QA after UI changes
  • Chrome DevTools MCP — debugging, not just driving pages
  • Linear or Jira — tickets from findings
  • GitLab — if that is your host (browse coding-agent MCP for more)

Install HTTP Discovery in Claude Code with:

claude mcp add --transport http influzer-discovery \
  https://www.influzer.ai/mcp/discovery

If your CLI build rejects the flag, use the Desktop/web connector for the same URL — do not fork the server. Details: CLI vs Desktop connectors.

Data & memory

  • PostgreSQL — any Postgres URL with least-privilege credentials
  • Neon — when you need Neon platform tools, not only SQL
  • Notion — team docs and databases
  • Memory — local knowledge graph for persistent agent state

Prefer read-only DB roles until you have an audit trail. Use-case hubs: RAG MCP.

Setup checklist

  1. Decide which Claude surface you are installing for — web connectors cannot run stdio.
  2. Add Discovery first so Claude can search the rest of the catalog from chat.
  3. Install a remote starter set (Context7 + one data or monitoring tool) if you live on claude.ai.
  4. Add research/coding stdio servers only on Desktop or Claude Code.
  5. Verify with a small prompt (tools/list, one URL fetch, one SELECT) before wider rollout.
  6. Run the seven-question MCP audit before production write tools.

How to choose (cheat sheet)

  • Only Claude.ai? Filter for remote/HTTP. Discovery, Context7, Neon, Sentry are a proven set.
  • Live in Claude Code? Stdio is fine — Firecrawl, Playwright, Postgres are common.
  • Do not install Exa and Brave Search on day one — pick one search tool, add a scraper if you need full pages.
  • OAuth-gated vendors (many hosted gateways) will reject anonymous tools/list probes — that is expected; use their connector OAuth flow, not a public probe.

Quick answers

What are the best MCP servers for Claude overall?

Start with Discovery + Context7 + one web tool (Exa or Firecrawl) + one data or issue tracker. Expand only when a workflow is blocked.

Can Claude.ai use local MCP servers?

No. Custom connectors only call public HTTPS endpoints. Local stdio works in Desktop and Claude Code.

Is Influzer Discovery free?

Yes — public read-only HTTPS, no API key. Setup: /mcp/discovery/setup.

Where do I browse alternatives?

Top 100, full directory, and topic guides (browser automation, RAG, coding agents, scraping).

How is this different from "works in Cursor"?

Cursor can run local stdio next to the repo. Claude.ai cannot. Treat remote HTTPS as the org path — see three surfaces.

Bottom line

The best MCP stack for Claude is the one that matches your surface. Remote connectors for claude.ai. Stdio where Desktop and Code allow it. Discovery first so you stop guessing from a static Top 10 blog post.

Connect Discovery once. Ask Claude to shortlist. Install only what the workflow needs.
